statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00Z on Friday and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon, which ends about seven hours before the scheduled Sunday reopen. Stress is 41, moderate: a 50% US tariff on Canadian goods is in force, Ottawa has suspended talks and dated a dollar-for-dollar match to 8 September, the H.15 curve stands at 4.19% on the 2-year, 4.69% on the 10-year and 5.23% on the 30-year with the long end at its highest since 2007, and next week carries PCE, Nvidia's results and a first Jackson Hole keynote from the current Fed Chair. Confidence is 87, high, because the closed-venue fact is verified and the supporting levels, yields, volatility, energy and calendar were all checked against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, reclaimed the entire decline to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, below its own open, while VIX settled at 14.89 near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. Both extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so no Tail amplifier from observed structure is present. Because the venue is shut, no hour in this horizon can generate the shallow-pullback or extreme-holding behaviour that would move Tail toward the block threshold, and Tail therefore stays at its closed-venue floor while Stress carries the unpriced policy and rates stack. The danger window is empty by construction: there is no tradable interval inside the published horizon.
headline: Closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across all twenty-four published hours while a 50% US tariff on Canadian goods meets a matching response now dated to 8 September, a 30-year yield at its highest since 2007 sits unpriced, and Tail holds the closed-venue floor of 4.
body: CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run from 2026-08-22T16:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T15:00:00Z and end roughly seven hours before that reopen. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, printing a 29,142.44 low and a 29,405.12 high; both extremes were retraced inside the session and the close finished below the open, which is the shape of a market that still mean-reverts. The week as a whole was negative, with the S&P 500 down 1.4% and the Nasdaq Composite down 2%, and VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00%, near the bottom of a 14.77-15.95 range rather than at a stressed extreme. The dominant unpriced item is trade policy. Talks between Washington and Ottawa collapsed shortly before a midnight deadline and a 50% US tariff took effect on Canadian goods, with the affected trade reported at about $20bn by NPR and about $28bn by Yahoo Finance. Prime Minister Carney suspended negotiations and said Canada will match the measure dollar for dollar from 8 September, so the retaliation is now dated and sits well beyond this horizon rather than hanging over the reopen as an open-ended threat; that dating is the reason Stress eases one point to 41 rather than holding at 42. The rates channel remains the most credible route to a genuinely difficult tape. The latest H.15 daily figures put the 2-year at 4.19%, the 10-year at 4.69% and the 30-year at 5.23%, and Friday's intraday move carried the long end toward 5.27% and the 10-year toward 4.73% after the Treasury's expanded buyback failed to hold yields down, with reporting on Friday putting a market-implied probability near 35% on a September rate hike. Energy is contained for now, with WTI at $87.06, up 0.26% inside an $85.80-$87.51 range, though the announced US economic-isolation campaign against Iran and the port blockade keep a premium in place; the detail briefing on that campaign falls on Monday, after this forecast expires. Friday's leadership was dispersed rather than aligned, with Tesla up 5.14%, Alphabet up 1.22% and Broadcom up 1.21% against Nvidia down 0.98%, Apple down 0.63% and Amazon down 0.57%, and a mixed semiconductor cohort; delayed cross-asset context also showed index futures modestly higher and the volatility future lower on the latest session, which is supporting context only and not evidence of a live price path. Next week concentrates the catalysts: PCE with the second Q2 GDP estimate on Wednesday, Nvidia's results after that session's close, and the Jackson Hole symposium from Thursday with the Fed Chair keynote on Friday. None of that can be observed inside this horizon, so every forecast hour treats it as a conditional checkpoint and Tail stays at the closed-venue floor while Stress reflects how much has accumulated without a market able to price it.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is close to complete: 22 hourly assessments are available, while the 05:00Z and 06:00Z clock-hours on 22 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout, so no hour approached the block threshold. The path tracks the transition from a live Friday session, where Tail ran 13-16 and Stress 53-55 with a mixed dominant mode, into the futures halt at 21:00Z, after which Tail fell to the closed-venue floor of 4 and the dominant mode settled to normal. Stress fell with the halt to 35-36 overnight and then rebuilt to 42 through Saturday as the tariff step took effect, before easing to 41 in the current hour once the Canadian response was dated to 8 September. Confidence stayed in an 84-88 band throughout.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the final slot begins at 2026-08-23T15:00:00Z and ends about seven hours before the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds 4 in every hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON, with the danger window empty because no tradable interval exists inside the horizon. Stress eases from 41 to 40 through the quiet Saturday evening and overnight hours, then rebuilds to 44 by the final slot as the reopen approaches with the tariff step, a 2007-high long end, the unresolved Iran campaign and next week's PCE, Nvidia and Jackson Hole checkpoints all still unpriced. Confidence decays from 87 to 81 across the horizon purely because the verified evidence ages while no session can refresh it. Any statement about opening structure at the reopen would be conditional; this horizon contains no hour in which such structure could be observed.
